title: An Atlantic chapter
text: Postwar hardship and established family networks encouraged emigration from the Canary Islands to Venezuela. This regional story belongs within Spain; national migration estimates cannot isolate island departures.

title: Recruiting for reconstruction
text: The December 1955 recruitment agreement opened a formal route for Italian workers to West Germany. Postwar demand for labor shaped new migration networks.

title: Flight after the uprising
text: The Hungarian uprising and Soviet repression in October and November 1956 forced people to seek safety across the Austrian border.

title: A new labor corridor
text: The recruitment agreement of 30 October 1961 connected Turkish workers with West German employers. Family and community networks would give this migration a lasting significance.

title: Independence and departure
text: Algerian independence was accompanied by departures to France. European settlers and threatened Algerians, including harkis and their families, faced different circumstances and risks.

title: Expelled from home
text: The August 1972 expulsion of Ugandan Asians forced families to leave. Many found refuge in the United Kingdom.

title: Decolonization and evacuation
text: Angolan independence and escalating conflict prompted departures and an evacuation airlift to Portugal. Colonial ties shaped the route.

title: Life under martial law
text: Martial law imposed on 13 December 1981 and political repression accompanied emigration from Poland, including to West Germany.

title: Borders and possibilities
text: The Romanian revolution and the end of restrictions on mobility changed opportunities to move. Germany became a significant destination during the following years.

title: Displaced by war
text: War in Bosnia and Herzegovina forced people to seek safety across Europe, including in Germany. Displacement, temporary protection and later returns shaped these journeys.

title: Across a shared language
text: Colombia’s 1998–1999 economic crisis, Spanish employment opportunities and a shared language contributed to increased emigration to Spain. This was a combination of pressures and opportunities, rather than a single starting point.

title: An enlarged Europe
text: EU enlargement on 1 May 2004 and access to the UK labor market created new opportunities for Polish workers and families.

title: Looking for opportunity
text: The financial and employment crisis accompanied renewed migration from Spain to Germany. Work, family ties and individual circumstances influenced decisions.

title: Seeking safety
text: Civil war in Syria forced millions from their homes. Germany became an important European destination, with substantial arrivals later in this period.

title: A changing eastern border
text: Russian aggression beginning in 2014 and associated economic deterioration intensified migration from Ukraine to Poland. Work and existing networks also shaped the corridor.

title: A deepening crisis
text: Political, economic and humanitarian crisis contributed to an escalating Venezuelan migration wave. Spain was one destination; migration on this route predates the crisis.

title: Beyond the border
text: Following the August 2020 election and repression in Belarus, migration to Poland intensified. The Polish Office for Foreigners identifies increased residence applications after the election and again after the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Its permit and protection figures describe administrative measures, not direct migration counts.

title: Forced to leave
text: Russia’s full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022 triggered large-scale displacement. Poland welcomed people fleeing Ukraine. Border crossings and refugee registrations are distinct from the modelled migration estimates on this map.

title: Political, economic and humanitarian crisis
text: The recent Venezuelan exodus intensified from 2014 during a prolonged political, economic and humanitarian crisis. UNHCR documented people leaving amid insecurity and violence, loss of income, and shortages of food, medicines and essential services. These country-wide pressures provide context for emigration to different destinations; individual circumstances and routes vary. This featured period does not mark the beginning of all Venezuelan migration or assign the selected migration total to a single cause.

title: Election uncertainty and mobility constraints
text: R4V reported renewed uncertainty and heightened tension following the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election. Interruptions affecting diplomatic and consular access and travel created difficulties with documentation, family reunification and protection. This is context for Venezuelan outward movement during 2024, rather than a quantified explanation for a particular destination or for earlier migration.

title: War and displacement from Sudan
text: Armed conflict beginning in April 2023 forced people from their homes within Sudan and across borders, including to Chad, Egypt, South Sudan and other neighbouring countries. These movements include refugees and people returning to their own countries; they are not equivalent to a particular bilateral migration total.

title: Political upheaval and humanitarian crisis
text: Conflict and the August 2021 takeover, economic deterioration and drought contributed to displacement in and from Afghanistan. Experiences and destinations differ; the context does not assign the migration figures to a specific cause.

title: Conflict and displacement from Syria
text: The Syrian conflict forced people to seek safety inside Syria and in neighbouring countries, with some later moving onward. UNHCR documented more than four million Syrian refugees in neighbouring countries by July 2015. Refugee counts and annual migration flows are different measures.

title: Full-scale invasion and displacement
text: Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022 caused large-scale displacement within Ukraine and across borders. Many people fled to neighbouring countries and elsewhere in Europe. Border crossings and refugee registrations do not equal long-term bilateral migration flows.
